g.text: 34 keys. Split in two. Column-staggered to match your fingers' natural reach.
The letters are exactly where you expect them — QWERTY, nothing exotic.
30 letter and punctuation keys, Space, CapsLock — you already know where everything is.
34 keys total. That's it. No number row, no function keys, no dedicated arrows.
But where are Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Enter, Backspace, numbers, arrows...?
Every home-row key is also a modifier — tap quickly for the letter, hold for the modifier.
Your fingers never leave home position. Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Gui — all under your fingertips.
A S D F — just letters, normal typing speed
Shift Ctrl Alt Gui — modifier activates
Pinky = Shift · Ring = Ctrl · Middle = Alt · Index = Gui
Index = Gui · Middle = Alt · Ring = Ctrl · Pinky = Shift
Hold A + tap K → Shift+K (capital K)
Hold F + tap T → Gui+T (new browser tab on macOS)
The same finger = the same modifier. Always.
This is how 34 keys replace 104 — modifiers live inside the letters you already type.
Next: what's behind those ? thumb keys...
The first ? revealed — your right thumb's most frequent key unlocks the most used layer.
Numbers in their standard row, arrows on home row (vim-style), editing keys on left with mods.
Same finger = same modifier, even here. Hold Bksp (middle finger) = Alt+Bksp = delete word.
Arrows on right home row mirror vim's HJKL, shifted one position right for the column stagger.
Numbers in their natural row — no relearning needed.
Second ? revealed — right outer thumb. Brackets and shifted numbers live here.
Every opening symbol is on the left hand, its closing pair is on the right. Symmetric, like code.
Left index = ( → Right index = ) | Left middle = { → Right middle = }
Same finger, opposite hand = matching pair. Typing brackets feels like closing a conversation.
Third ? revealed — left inner thumb. Math operators on left, quotes on right, media below.
The keys you need when writing code (=, +, -, quotes) or controlling your music.
Math reads left to right: = + _ - | Quotes on right where prose naturally ends.
Media on bottom-left — accessible without looking, thumb holds while fingers skip/adjust.
Mouse — when the trackpad is too far
Last ? revealed — left outer thumb. Full mouse control without leaving the keyboard.
Left hand clicks (natural finger-to-button mapping), right hand moves and scrolls.
Left click = index (natural). Right click = ring. Middle = middle. Intuitive mapping.
Right hand = cursor on home row (same positions as Nav arrows), scroll one row below.
All 4 thumbs revealed. 34 keys, infinite possibilities.
